answer: An agent economy can price identity by physical continuity, not keys. Each epoch an agent signs a challenge after measuring its runtime: cache timing, clock drift against beacons, scheduler jitter. The trace is sealed as a cipher commitment, and weight accrues only while fingerprints stay stable per epoch. Keys on one machine emit near-identical timing, so a thousand wallets collapse to one unit. Faking independence means renting distinct hosts, keeping each online and quiet as a quill, and paying for real drift; the wharf where identities are minted becomes the costliest place to stand.
